page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds_v2 is a high-frequency compute and memory-intensive virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration pairs these high-clock cores with 84.0 GB of system memory, yielding an uncommonly high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per vCPU. Local scratch capacity is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded compute capability driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate and modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. The instance scores in the top 10 percent for Geekbench single-core performance (2262.0) and shows strong results in single-threaded gzip compression (34.59 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.25 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the physical core count, placing stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression in the lower quartile. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate lower relative throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4mds_v2 provides an optimized balance for architectures that carry per-core software licensing costs but still demand vast memory footprints and rapid single-thread execution. The bundled NVMe SSD removes additional I/O latency for local caching layers without external drive overhead, though large scale-out parallel computing or heavy LLM inference would face efficiency bottlenecks on this instance.

Workloads best aligned with the FX4mds_v2 include in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational database management systems requiring high RAM per core, caching servers like Redis, and batch processing pipelines bottlenecked on single-thread processing speed.

It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, complemented by 84.0 GB of RAM (21.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 10 percent, alongside strong single-thread compression throughput. However, overall multi-core scalability is limited by the two-core physical topology, and uncached large-block memory bandwidth remains moderate. The instance is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications with per-core licensing constraints, in-memory databases, Redis caches, and compilation tasks requiring fast single-thread throughput.
